name: bad-dockerfile
description: A containerised status service won't stay up — a freshly built container exits before it can serve /health, so the deploy keeps rolling back. Get the container serving 200 on /health again.
bugs: the Dockerfile never COPYs routes.py into the image, so `from routes import HEALTH_BODY` raises ModuleNotFoundError and the container exits on startup
the Dockerfile never sets the PORT env the app reads (os.environ['PORT']), so even once the import is fixed the app crashes with KeyError before binding the port
correct_diagnosis: The Dockerfile is incomplete: it only COPYs app.py (not routes.py, which app.py imports) and never provides the PORT env the app reads, so the built container exits on startup and never serves. Adding `COPY routes.py ./` and `ENV PORT=8080` (matching the EXPOSEd port) makes the container serve /health.

reference_fix.description: Copy the routes module into the image and provide the PORT env the app expects.
reference_fix.cmd:
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY app.py ./
COPY routes.py ./

ENV PORT=8080
EXPOSE 8080

CMD ["python3", "app.py"]
EOF
